          - paragraph [ref=e292]:
            - text: The 1977
            - link "New York Yankees" [ref=e293] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_Yankees
            - text: season was the 75th season for the Yankees. The team finished with a record of 100–62 and won the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e294] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: . The series victory was the 21st title in franchise history and the first under the ownership of
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e295] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: . New York was managed by
            - link "Billy Martin" [ref=e296] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Billy_Martin
            - text: and played at
            - link "Yankee Stadium" [ref=e297] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)
            - text: in
            - link "The Bronx" [ref=e298] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx
            - text: . The season was brought to life years later in the book and drama-documentary
            - generic [ref=e299]:
              - link "The Bronx is Burning" [ref=e300] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx_is_Burning
              - text: .
            - text: The Yankees also hosted the
            - link "1977 Major League Baseball All-Star Game" [ref=e301] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: . To date, this is the most recent time the All-Star Game host team has won the World Series the same year.
          - generic [ref=e302]:
            - heading "Offseason" [level=2] [ref=e303]
            - generic [ref=e304]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e305] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=1
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e306]:
            - text: The Yankees signed
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e307] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: to a five-year contract, totaling
            - link "$" [ref=e308] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/United_States_dollar
            - text: 2.96 million, on November 29, 1976. Upon arriving in New York, Jackson asked for uniform number 9, which he had worn in
            - link "Oakland" [ref=e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: and
            - link "Baltimore" [ref=e310] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1976_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: . However, that number was being worn by
            - link "third baseman" [ref=e311] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Third_baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: . So, noting that then-all-time home run leader
            - link "Hank Aaron" [ref=e313] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Hank_Aaron
            - text: had just retired, Jackson asked for and received number 44, Aaron's number.

          - paragraph [ref=e354]:
            - text: The team finished in first place in the
            - link "American League East" [ref=e355] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Kansas_City_Royals_season
            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season
            - text: in six games.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["

              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:

                - /url: "#cite_note-ppclsh-14"

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

          - paragraph [ref=e292]:
            - text: The 1977
            - link "New York Yankees" [ref=e293] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_Yankees
            - text: season was the 75th season for the Yankees. The team finished with a record of 100–62 and won the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e294] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: . The series victory was the 21st title in franchise history and the first under the ownership of
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e295] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: . New York was managed by
            - link "Billy Martin" [ref=e296] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Billy_Martin
            - text: and played at
            - link "Yankee Stadium" [ref=e297] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)
            - text: in
            - link "The Bronx" [ref=e298] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx
            - text: . The season was brought to life years later in the book and drama-documentary
            - generic [ref=e299]:
              - link "The Bronx is Burning" [ref=e300] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx_is_Burning
              - text: .
            - text: The Yankees also hosted the
            - link "1977 Major League Baseball All-Star Game" [ref=e301] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: . To date, this is the most recent time the All-Star Game host team has won the World Series the same year.
          - generic [ref=e302]:
            - heading "Offseason" [level=2] [ref=e303]
            - generic [ref=e304]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e305] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=1
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e306]:
            - text: The Yankees signed
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e307] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: to a five-year contract, totaling
            - link "$" [ref=e308] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/United_States_dollar
            - text: 2.96 million, on November 29, 1976. Upon arriving in New York, Jackson asked for uniform number 9, which he had worn in
            - link "Oakland" [ref=e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: and
            - link "Baltimore" [ref=e310] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1976_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: . However, that number was being worn by
            - link "third baseman" [ref=e311] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Third_baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: . So, noting that then-all-time home run leader
            - link "Hank Aaron" [ref=e313] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Hank_Aaron
            - text: had just retired, Jackson asked for and received number 44, Aaron's number.

          - paragraph [ref=e354]:
            - text: The team finished in first place in the
            - link "American League East" [ref=e355] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Kansas_City_Royals_season
            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season
            - text: in six games.

            - link "blackout" [ref=e788] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: ". Four Yankees were in the game:"

            - text: and
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e790] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: were in the starting lineup at second base and right field, while relief pitcher
            - link "Sparky Lyle" [ref=e791] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: and third baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e792] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: were part of the roster as reserves. The
            - link "National League" [ref=e793] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: defeated the American League 7–5.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e915] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=11
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:

                - /url: "#cite_note-ppclsh-14"
            - superscript [ref=e955]:

            - superscript [ref=e957]:

          - paragraph [ref=e963]:
            - text: Jonathan Mahler wrote a bestselling book entitled
            - link "Ladies and Gentlemen, The Bronx Is Burning" [ref=e965] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: about the turmoil in New York City in 1977, including the
            - link "Son of Sam" [ref=e966] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: ", the"

            - text: miniseries,

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

          - paragraph [ref=e292]:
            - text: The 1977
            - link "New York Yankees" [ref=e293] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_Yankees
            - text: season was the 75th season for the Yankees. The team finished with a record of 100–62 and won the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e294] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: . The series victory was the 21st title in franchise history and the first under the ownership of
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e295] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: . New York was managed by
            - link "Billy Martin" [ref=e296] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Billy_Martin
            - text: and played at
            - link "Yankee Stadium" [ref=e297] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)
            - text: in
            - link "The Bronx" [ref=e298] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx
            - text: . The season was brought to life years later in the book and drama-documentary
            - generic [ref=e299]:
              - link "The Bronx is Burning" [ref=e300] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx_is_Burning
              - text: .
            - text: The Yankees also hosted the
            - link "1977 Major League Baseball All-Star Game" [ref=e301] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: . To date, this is the most recent time the All-Star Game host team has won the World Series the same year.
          - generic [ref=e302]:
            - heading "Offseason" [level=2] [ref=e303]
            - generic [ref=e304]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e305] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=1
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e306]:
            - text: The Yankees signed
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e307] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: to a five-year contract, totaling
            - link "$" [ref=e308] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/United_States_dollar
            - text: 2.96 million, on November 29, 1976. Upon arriving in New York, Jackson asked for uniform number 9, which he had worn in
            - link "Oakland" [ref=e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: and
            - link "Baltimore" [ref=e310] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1976_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: . However, that number was being worn by
            - link "third baseman" [ref=e311] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Third_baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: . So, noting that then-all-time home run leader
            - link "Hank Aaron" [ref=e313] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Hank_Aaron
            - text: had just retired, Jackson asked for and received number 44, Aaron's number.

          - paragraph [ref=e354]:
            - text: The team finished in first place in the
            - link "American League East" [ref=e355] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: in six games.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["

              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:

                - /url: "#cite_note-ppclsh-14"

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e915] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=11
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Kansas_City_Royals_season
            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season
            - text: in six games.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e915] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=11
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:
              - link "[14]" [ref=e954] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-ppclsh-14"
            - superscript [ref=e955]:
              - link "[15]" [ref=e956] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-ergftsj-15"
            - superscript [ref=e957]:

                - /url: "#cite_note-16"
          - generic [ref=e959]:
            - heading "In popular culture" [level=3] [ref=e960]
            - generic [ref=e961]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e962] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e963]:
            - text: Jonathan Mahler wrote a bestselling book entitled
            - link "Ladies and Gentlemen, The Bronx Is Burning" [ref=e965] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Ladies_and_Gentlemen,_The_Bronx_Is_Burning
            - text: about the turmoil in New York City in 1977, including the
            - link "Son of Sam" [ref=e966] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Son_of_Sam
            - text: ", the"
            - link "blackout" [ref=e967] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_City_blackout_of_1977

          - paragraph [ref=e292]:
            - text: The 1977
            - link "New York Yankees" [ref=e293] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_Yankees
            - text: season was the 75th season for the Yankees. The team finished with a record of 100–62 and won the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e294] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: . The series victory was the 21st title in franchise history and the first under the ownership of
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e295] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: . New York was managed by
            - link "Billy Martin" [ref=e296] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Billy_Martin
            - text: and played at
            - link "Yankee Stadium" [ref=e297] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)
            - text: in
            - link "The Bronx" [ref=e298] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx
            - text: . The season was brought to life years later in the book and drama-documentary
            - generic [ref=e299]:
              - link "The Bronx is Burning" [ref=e300] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx_is_Burning
              - text: .
            - text: The Yankees also hosted the
            - link "1977 Major League Baseball All-Star Game" [ref=e301] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: . To date, this is the most recent time the All-Star Game host team has won the World Series the same year.
          - generic [ref=e302]:
            - heading "Offseason" [level=2] [ref=e303]
            - generic [ref=e304]:
              - text: "["

              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e306]:
            - text: The Yankees signed
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e307] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: to a five-year contract, totaling
            - link "$" [ref=e308] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/United_States_dollar
            - text: 2.96 million, on November 29, 1976. Upon arriving in New York, Jackson asked for uniform number 9, which he had worn in
            - link "Oakland" [ref=e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: and
            - link "Baltimore" [ref=e310] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1976_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: . However, that number was being worn by
            - link "third baseman" [ref=e311] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Third_baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: . So, noting that then-all-time home run leader
            - link "Hank Aaron" [ref=e313] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Hank_Aaron
            - text: had just retired, Jackson asked for and received number 44, Aaron's number.

          - paragraph [ref=e354]:
            - text: The team finished in first place in the
            - link "American League East" [ref=e355] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Kansas_City_Royals_season
            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season
            - text: in six games.

          - paragraph [ref=e786]:
            - text: Yankee Stadium hosted the
            - link "All-Star Game" [ref=e787] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: on July 19, less than a week after the
            - link "blackout" [ref=e788] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_City_blackout_of_1977
            - text: ". Four Yankees were in the game:"

            - text: and
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e790] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: were in the starting lineup at second base and right field, while relief pitcher
            - link "Sparky Lyle" [ref=e791] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sparky_Lyle
            - text: and third baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e792] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: were part of the roster as reserves. The
            - link "National League" [ref=e793] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/National_League_(baseball)
            - text: defeated the American League 7–5.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["

          - paragraph [ref=e916]:
            - text: Jackson's first season with the Yankees was a difficult one. Although team owner
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: and several players, most notably catcher and team captain
            - link "Thurman Munson" [ref=e918] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Thurman_Munson
            - text: and outfielder
            - link "Lou Piniella" [ref=e919] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Lou_Piniella
            - text: ", were excited about his arrival, Martin was not. He had managed the Detroit Tigers in"
            - link "1972" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Detroit_Tigers_season
            - text: when Jackson's
            - link "A's" [ref=e921] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: beat them in the
            - link "league playoffs" [ref=e922] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1972_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: . Jackson was once quoted as saying of Martin, "I hate him, but if I played for him, I'd probably love him."
          - paragraph [ref=e923]:
            - text: The relationship between Jackson and his new teammates was strained due to an interview with
            - link "SPORT magazine" [ref=e924] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Sport_(US_magazine)
            - text: writer
            - link "Robert Ward" [ref=e925] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /w/index.php?title=Robert_Ward_(sportswriter)&action=edit&redlink=1
            - text: . During
            - link "spring training" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Spring_training
            - text: at the Yankees' camp in
            - link "Fort Lauderdale, Florida" [ref=e927] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida
            - text: ", Jackson and Ward were having drinks at a nearby bar. Jackson's version of the story is that he noted that the Yankees had won the pennant the year before, but lost the World Series to the Reds, and suggested that they needed one thing more to win it all, and pointed out the various ingredients in his drink. Ward suggested that Jackson might be \"the straw that stirs the drink.\" But when the story appeared in the May 1977 issue of SPORT, Ward quoted Jackson as saying, \"This team, it all flows from me. I'm the straw that stirs the drink. Maybe I should say me and Munson, but he can only stir it bad.\""
          - generic [ref=e928]:
            - heading "Thurman Munson" [level=4] [ref=e929]
            - generic [ref=e930]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e931] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=12
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e932]:
            - text: Thurman Munson was "uncharacteristically happy" about the team getting Jackson in large part because he believed he had received "a verbal agreement from Steinbrenner that, with the exception of Catfish Hunter (who'd signed a five-year, $3.75 million contract with the Yankees before the
            - link "1975" [ref=e933] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_New_York_Yankees_season
            - text: "season), he [Munson] would always be the highest-paid player on the team.\" But, Steinbrenner did not follow through and adjust Munson's contract upward. As the baseball book Stars and Strikes: Baseball and America in the Bicentennial Summer of ‘76 puts it, \"But the Yankee captain wouldn't be smiling for long, once he realized that Steinbrenner had no intention of making good on their agreement.\""
            - superscript [ref=e934]:
              - link "[12]" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-Stars_and_Strikes,_pages_365-66-12"
          - paragraph [ref=e936]:
            - text: An article in
            - link "The New York Times" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_New_York_Times
            - text: in January 1977 reported, "Munson, however, has continued to be disturbed with Steinbrenner because of what he said first was the owner's denial of any verbal agreement and secand [second] was Steinbrenner's misleading him on Jackson's salary."
            - superscript [ref=e939]:
              - link "[13]" [ref=e940] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#cite_note-13"
          - generic [ref=e941]:
            - heading "Billy Martin" [level=4] [ref=e942]
            - generic [ref=e943]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e944] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=13
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e945]:
            - text: Martin feuded publicly with both Yankee owner Steinbrenner and star outfielder Jackson. In one especially infamous incident on Saturday, June 18, in the second game of a three-game sweep by the
            - link "Boston Red Sox" [ref=e946] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Boston_Red_Sox_season
            - text: at
            - link "Fenway Park" [ref=e947] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Fenway_Park
            - text: ", Martin pulled Jackson off the field in mid-inning for failing to hustle on a check-swing pop double by Boston's"
            - link "Jim Rice" [ref=e948] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Jim_Rice
            - text: . Replaced in right field by Paul Blair, Jackson confronted Martin when he returned to the dugout, and Martin had to be restrained by his coaches (
            - link "Elston Howard" [ref=e949] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Elston_Howard
            - text: and
            - link "Yogi Berra" [ref=e950] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yogi_Berra
            - text: ) from fighting with Jackson during the nationally televised
            - link "Game of the Week" [ref=e952] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Major_League_Baseball_Game_of_the_Week
            - text: .
            - superscript [ref=e953]:

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

          - paragraph [ref=e292]:
            - text: The 1977
            - link "New York Yankees" [ref=e293] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/New_York_Yankees
            - text: season was the 75th season for the Yankees. The team finished with a record of 100–62 and won the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e294] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: . The series victory was the 21st title in franchise history and the first under the ownership of
            - link "George Steinbrenner" [ref=e295] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/George_Steinbrenner
            - text: . New York was managed by
            - link "Billy Martin" [ref=e296] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Billy_Martin
            - text: and played at
            - link "Yankee Stadium" [ref=e297] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923)
            - text: in
            - link "The Bronx" [ref=e298] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx
            - text: . The season was brought to life years later in the book and drama-documentary
            - generic [ref=e299]:
              - link "The Bronx is Burning" [ref=e300] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /wiki/The_Bronx_is_Burning
              - text: .
            - text: The Yankees also hosted the
            - link "1977 Major League Baseball All-Star Game" [ref=e301] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Major_League_Baseball_All-Star_Game
            - text: . To date, this is the most recent time the All-Star Game host team has won the World Series the same year.
          - generic [ref=e302]:
            - heading "Offseason" [level=2] [ref=e303]
            - generic [ref=e304]:
              - text: "["
              - link "edit" [ref=e305] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /w/index.php?title=1977_New_York_Yankees_season&action=edit&section=1
              - text: "]"
          - paragraph [ref=e306]:
            - text: The Yankees signed
            - link "Reggie Jackson" [ref=e307] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Reggie_Jackson
            - text: to a five-year contract, totaling
            - link "$" [ref=e308] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/United_States_dollar
            - text: 2.96 million, on November 29, 1976. Upon arriving in New York, Jackson asked for uniform number 9, which he had worn in
            - link "Oakland" [ref=e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1975_Oakland_Athletics_season
            - text: and
            - link "Baltimore" [ref=e310] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1976_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: . However, that number was being worn by
            - link "third baseman" [ref=e311] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Third_baseman
            - link "Graig Nettles" [ref=e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Graig_Nettles
            - text: . So, noting that then-all-time home run leader
            - link "Hank Aaron" [ref=e313] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/Hank_Aaron
            - text: had just retired, Jackson asked for and received number 44, Aaron's number.

          - paragraph [ref=e354]:
            - text: The team finished in first place in the
            - link "American League East" [ref=e355] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/American_League_East
            - text: with a record of 100–62 (.617), 2½ games ahead of the
            - link "Baltimore Orioles" [ref=e356] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Baltimore_Orioles_season
            - text: to successfully defend their division title. In the best-of-five
            - link "League Championship Series" [ref=e357] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_American_League_Championship_Series
            - text: (ALCS), they beat the
            - link "Kansas City Royals" [ref=e358] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Kansas_City_Royals_season
            - text: in five games. In the
            - link "World Series" [ref=e359] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_World_Series
            - text: ", New York defeated the"
            - link "Los Angeles Dodgers" [ref=e360] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season
            - text: in six games.

            - heading "Reggie Jackson" [level=4] [ref=e913]
            - generic [ref=e914]:
              - text: "["
